When to use the SDK

orca-harness-sdk is the high-level Rust facade for embedding Orca Harness in your own process. It composes models, workspace tools, extensions, sessions, memory, skills, MCP, events, retries, truncation, compaction, and cancellation without importing the orcacode terminal UI or its configuration layer.

HOST RESPONSIBILITY

The SDK executes with the permissions of your process. Your application owns credential loading, user-facing approvals, configuration, process isolation, shutdown policy, and which tools it exposes. ToolPreset::Coding and ToolPreset::ShellLess can change workspace state; do not enable them for untrusted prompts without an appropriate policy and sandbox.

ChooseWhen
orca-harness-sdkYou want a batteries-included Rust composition API with sessions and common extensions.
orca-harness-coreYou need direct control over the minimal model → tool loop and will assemble every lifecycle component yourself.
orcacodeYou want the ready-made interactive or headless terminal host rather than an embedded library.

Add the crate

The SDK is currently a workspace crate. From a checkout of this repository, add it by path:

$ cargo add --path crates/sdk orca-harness-sdk
$ cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread

In Cargo.toml, package names use hyphens while Rust imports use underscores:

[dependencies]
orca-harness-sdk = { path = "crates/sdk" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
VERSIONING

The facade is at 0.1.0. Pin the exact revision when consuming it from outside this workspace and expect the API to evolve before a stable release.

Build and run an agent

A Harness owns workspace-scoped paths. An Agent is a reusable definition. A Session owns conversation context, and each run adds one user turn.

use orca_harness_sdk::{Harness, OpenAiModel, ToolPreset};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let model = OpenAiModel::new("gpt-4o-mini")
        .api_key(std::env::var("OPENAI_API_KEY")?);

    let harness = Harness::builder()
        .workspace(std::env::current_dir()?)
        .build()?;

    let agent = harness
        .agent(model)
        .name("embedded-assistant")
        .system_prompt("Be concise. Inspect before changing files.")
        .tools(ToolPreset::ReadOnly)
        .build()?;

    let session = agent.new_session().ephemeral().open()?;
    let result = session.run("Summarize this workspace").await?;
    println!("{}", result.text);
    Ok(())
}

HarnessBuilder::workspace defaults to the current directory. The directory must already exist and is canonicalized. State defaults to <workspace>/.orca; call .state_dir(...) to keep SDK state elsewhere.

Supply a model

Harness::agent accepts any implementation of the re-exported Model trait. The facade re-exports the built-in OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, and OpenAI Codex adapters.

AdapterConstruction
OpenAI or compatible endpointOpenAiModel::new("model").api_key(key); add .base_url(url) for vLLM, llama.cpp, or another compatible server.
OpenRouterOpenRouterModel::new("provider/model").api_key(key).
ChatGPT/Codex credentialsOpenAiCodexModel::new("model", credential_source). This constructor expects Arc<dyn CodexCredentialSource>. That trait is not re-exported by the SDK, so Codex hosts must also depend on orca-harness-model-providers and import openai_codex::CodexCredentialSource. The host owns credential acquisition, persistence, and refresh.
Custom or test modelImplement Model. Repository examples use ScriptedModel for deterministic, offline runs.

Credentials are plain host inputs to these adapters. The SDK does not read Orcacode’s saved config or start an interactive login flow.

Choose tools explicitly

PresetCapabilities
ToolPreset::NoneNo workspace tools. This is the default.
ToolPreset::ReadOnlyRead files, list directories, grep, and glob.
ToolPreset::ShellLessRead/write/edit and filesystem administration, but no shell or long-lived process tool.
ToolPreset::CodingThe core coding toolset, including state-changing and command execution capabilities.

Add host-specific tools with .tool(...) or .tool_arc(...). FnTool is convenient for a typed JSON-schema boundary:

use orca_harness_sdk::FnTool;
use serde_json::json;

let lookup = FnTool::new(
    "lookup_issue",
    "Look up an issue by numeric id",
    json!({
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "id": { "type": "integer" } },
        "required": ["id"]
    }),
    |args, _context| async move {
        Ok(json!({ "id": args["id"], "status": "open" }))
    },
);

let agent = harness.agent(model).tool(lookup).build()?;

Use .python(), .bun(), and .todos() for the corresponding opt-in tools. Add ToolPolicy with .policy(policy) to allow or deny calls before execution.

Observe and control runs

Session::run waits for completion. Use RunRequest to attach images, a deadline, or an event callback. Events and usage metering are enabled by default.

use std::time::Duration;
use orca_harness_sdk::{HarnessEvent, RunRequest};

let request = RunRequest::new("Inspect the failing tests")
    .deadline(Duration::from_secs(90))
    .on_event(|event| {
        if let HarnessEvent::ToolCall { tool_name, .. } = event {
            eprintln!("calling {tool_name}");
        }
    });

let result = session.run(request).await?;
eprintln!("steps: {}", result.metered_steps);
eprintln!("tokens: {:?}", result.usage);
println!("{}", result.text);

RunResult contains final text, accumulated usage, metered model steps, and the resulting message list. RunRequest::image_path supports PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP files; image accepts an already encoded Image.

Background execution

Session::start returns a RunHandle with an event receiver, a cancellation token, and finish(). Dropping the handle requests cancellation. A session permits only one active run; concurrent use returns SdkError::BusySession.

let mut run = session.start("Run the analysis")?;
let cancel = run.cancellation_token();

while let Some(event) = run.events().recv().await {
    eprintln!("{event:?}");
    // Call cancel.cancel() from your timeout, signal, or UI handler.
}

let result = run.finish().await?;

Persist and branch sessions

Sessions are ephemeral unless .persistent() is selected. Persistent transcripts are stored below the harness state directory and can be listed and resumed by ID.

let session = agent.new_session().persistent().open()?;
let id = session.id().expect("persistent session id");
session.run("Review the current design").await?;

for file in harness.sessions().list() {
    println!("{} {}", file.meta.id, file.path.display());
}

let resumed = agent.resume_session(&id)?;
let branch = resumed.fork().await?;
MethodEffect
messages()Clone the current in-memory conversation.
fork()Create a persistent child session with inherited context and a new ID.
clear()Reset context and, for a persistent session, rotate to a new session file and ID.
reset_in_place()Destructively reset a persistent session while retaining its ID.
load_warnings()Report non-fatal warnings encountered while restoring persisted data.

Add memory, skills, and MCP

Memory

harness.memory() opens the workspace-scoped SQLite store. Use its CRUD methods directly, then attach a MemoryConfig to an agent. MemoryConfig::new enables automatic recall and the read-only search tool; MemoryConfig::read_write additionally exposes the management tool.

use orca_harness_sdk::MemoryConfig;

let memory = harness.memory()?;
memory.save("Prefer Rust examples", "preference", false, "host-setup")?;

let agent = harness
    .agent(model)
    .memory(MemoryConfig::new(memory).max_recalled_items(6))
    .build()?;

Skills

harness.skills() creates a manager for configured, home, and workspace roots. Call reload() before building the agent so discovered skills can become a tool. The manager also supports scaffold, install, enable, disable, and uninstall operations.

MCP

harness.mcp() creates an empty manager. Connect named stdio servers before passing the manager to the agent:

let mcp = harness.mcp();
let status = mcp.connect("tickets", "ticket-mcp --stdio").await?;
eprintln!("{} tools", status.tool_count);

let agent = harness.agent(model).mcp(mcp.clone()).build()?;
// Later: mcp.disconnect("tickets");

The command is launched as a local child process. Validate commands from configuration before connecting them, and arrange process cleanup appropriate to your host.

Harden long-running agents

Builder optionPurpose
tool_retry(RetryConfig)Retry transient tool failures.
model_retry(RetryConfig)Retry transient model failures.
truncation(TruncationConfig)Bound large string results, retain full data in a recovery store, and optionally expose read_tool_result.
automatic_compaction(threshold, tail)Compact context when estimated use reaches a percentage of context_capacity.
on_compact(callback)Observe automatic compaction reports.
limits(Limits)Bound model steps, tool calls, parallelism, and other kernel limits.

Truncation, event streaming, usage metering, and manual compaction support are configured by default. Call session.compact(CompactConfig { ... }) for explicit compaction. Persistent sessions also persist truncation recovery data so read_tool_result can recover full output after resume or fork.

Handle the SDK boundary

Public operations return SdkError. Match variants when the host can recover:

VariantTypical response
BusySessionWait for or cancel the active run; do not start a second turn on the same session.
SessionNotFoundRefresh the session list or create a new session.
EphemeralSessionUse a persistent session for fork or in-place reset operations that require a recorder.
HarnessInspect execution failures such as cancellation, deadlines, limits, model errors, or tool errors.
Io, Session, Memory, Mcp, SkillReport the owned subsystem failure without discarding its source.

Run the examples

The checked-in SDK examples use deterministic scripted models and temporary workspaces, so they require no API key or external network service.

$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example host_assembly
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example custom_tool_events
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example session_lifecycle
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example background_cancellation
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example memory_skills
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example local_mcp
$ cargo run -p orca-harness-sdk --example recovery_compaction_retry
ExampleFocus
host_assemblyComplete host composition: state, custom tool, policy, events, memory, skills, MCP, and persistence.
custom_tool_eventsCustom tool calls, ordered lifecycle events, and usage.
session_lifecycleList, resume, fork, clear-by-rotation, and reset-in-place.
background_cancellationBackground events, cooperative cancellation, and busy-session rejection.
memory_skillsMemory CRUD and recall plus the skill lifecycle.
local_mcpLocal stdio MCP discovery and connection lifecycle.
recovery_compaction_retryRetries, truncation recovery, resume/fork, and manual/automatic compaction.

For the broadest single-file walkthrough, also see crates/sdk/examples/agent_tour.rs. Validate all SDK targets with cargo test -p orca-harness-sdk and cargo clippy -p orca-harness-sdk --all-targets -- -D warnings.
